Hoping its not a dencun issue and just lack of validators it’s most likely just ppl not paying attention to their validators much. We see no issues in sepolia. just that its pinging on our alerts channel so often im likely to have to turn it off :/ yeah same if its just a poor quality network that's probably the answer though good thing you only have alerts for public testnets, you can imagine having notifications for all devnets too! the alerts for devnets has a name... barnabus 🙂 just dont watn to miss a mainnet issue because goerli is a basket case i guess I will send few thousands 1-blob txs to devnet-12 in the next 1-2h <@206016661470314496> ^ part of it is that the Nimbus fixes for the 24.1.2 Dencun regression were done, but for various reasons did not make it into fleet deployment for a while I'm currently trying to join the new Verkle testnet. When I attempt to join, I notice a difference between Besu and Geth in the way they calculate the hash of the genesis block. One aspect of this testnet is that the blobs start right from the genesis. Apparently, Geth ignores the blobGasUsed, excessBlobGas, and parentBeaconBlockRoot fields. In the case of the genesis, Geth don't include them at all in the RLP that it hash. Do we have a test that can verify on Hive that all clients behave the same way on a network that starts directly with Cancun? new verkle testnest doesn't have blobs it still running on top of shanghai ow ok I saw some blob links in the devnet 3 page and I was thinking that cancun is activated on it must be an oversigh by devops in their deployment template cc <@412614104222531604> ah yes we have no blobs, if you see any blob links its inherited from other playbooks, and there by mistake, I'll fix it. yes, why

excerpts.author: matkt0
excerpts.content: I'm currently trying to join the new Verkle testnet. When I attempt to join, I notice a difference between Besu and Geth in the way they calculate the hash of the genesis block. One aspect of this testnet is that the blobs start right from the genesis. Apparently, Geth ignores the blobGasUsed, excessBlobGas, and parentBeaconBlockRoot fields. In the case of the genesis, Geth don't include them at all in the RLP that it hash. Do we have a test that can verify on Hive that all clients behave the same way on a network that starts directly with Cancun?
